# Latest ombudsman data suggests promising signs despite increase in motor insurance complaints

Motor insurance continues to generate more complaints than any other insurance product, according to Insurance DataLab’s latest analysis of Financial Ombudsman Service (FOS) data, with complaints rising by almost 12% during the first quarter of 2026.

hits.title: Insurance complaints on the rise, says FCA | The Journal Magazine
hits.snippet:
“A key driver of the high level of complaints is the 18% increase in insurance-related complaints, particularly in motor insurance, alongside a continuing upward trend in complaints relating to disputed transactions in banking.”

Insurance complaints to the FSPO have increased by 18% since 2024, reaching 2,142 in 2025. This continues a longer-term trend, with complaints rising from 1,129 in 2022 to 2,142 in 2025 – almost doubling in just three years. [...] The FCA figures come a week after the Financial Services and Pensions Ombudsman (FSPO) published its Overview of Complaints 2025, highlighting continued growth in insurance-related complaints and increased scrutiny of provider practices.

Insurance continues to account for the second-largest share of complaints received by the FSPO (after banking), with 2,142 complaints in 2025. This represents 31% of all complaints received and reflects an 18% increase compared with 2024 (1,818). [...] The largest number of insurance complaints related to motor insurance (968 complaints), followed by private health insurance (325 complaints) and travel insurance (241 complaints).

Rising volumes

Dominic Harris, of the FSPO, said: “We resolved our highest ever number of complaints in 2025. The 6,282 complaints closed represent a 6% increase on the number closed in 2024 and a 34% increase on the number closed in 2022.
